chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: The Exclusive Club crowd and playing without a drummer
summary: Celebrities came less often than at the Yeah Man; he handled tempo for dancers and acted as the drummer.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How long does this go on with Willie Goat then, at the Exclusive?
I don't remember. It didn't go on too long.
Did celebrities come in there too?
Yeah. Just like the Yeah Man.
Yeah.
They used to come in there.
For the after hours club.
Yeah.
Yeah.
Not as frequently as they did at the Yeah Man, because the Yeah Man was right on 7th Avenue. Right on the main -- and the Exclusive Club was right off of 136th and right off of Lenox you know.
Yeah.
You had to -- I think you had to know about it.
Yeah.

And the other thing about playing with Willie (cont, your great thinger the tempo thing -- say with a tempos -- and you're playing with a pianist like this -- it must be rather difficult with a band -- I mean you're not playing for dances, are you?
No. Well, they used to -- you know, couples used to, you know, come up and dance. There was room for them to dance. And, they would dance.
Yeah.
So, we had to play tempo things, you know.
Yeah. Yeah.
And, most of the things I played with him -- I think some of the things -- I think -- maybe some of the numbers I laid out. Like -- if you remember
Yeah.
Yeah.
You know.
Yeah.
Yeah. And then I would go into -- whenever he'd wants to say 'stride'.
There were some records made by Spencer Williams and Teddy Bunn, piano and guitar.
Oh, yeah?
I wonder whether in those days -- did you ever hear of other people just playing piano and guitar in clubs like this?
No.
Well, I haven't either.
No, you know, and that's why I say I was a little concerned about, you know, whether this thing would go. I needed a job, you know.
Yeah.
And I wanted -- you know, after Lennie left -- or while Lennie was there, then --
Well, you mean Lennie had the job there for a while?
No. What I'm saying -- after -- as far as I'm concerned, as far as playing with a piano player --
Yeah?
I wondered how it would be if Lennie wasn't there to play that, tenor. You know what I mean?
To be --
Yeah.
In effect, you're putting some rhythm in for the
Yeah, you know what I mean? I like to hear that horn, you know?
Oh, Lennie Simmons.
No, no, no, no. But, I wondered about that myself, you know. How it would go. But, it went okay.
Another thing is, I mean, you don't have a drummer.
No.
And, so who's going to hold onto that beat?
I had to. I had to be the drummer also.
